quests.instruction: You are reading a picture book. Which body part do you use to look at the pictures?
quests.hint: You have two of them, and they sit just above your nose.
quests.explanation: Eyes take in light from the world around you, so you can see colors, shapes, and pictures.
quests.funFact: You blink about 15 to 20 times every minute, and each blink keeps your eyes moist.

quests.instruction: A flower is blooming in the garden. Which body part picks up its smell?
quests.hint: It sits in the middle of your face, just above your mouth.
quests.explanation: Your nose catches smells from the air, like flowers, fresh bread, or rain.
quests.funFact: Your nose also warms and cleans the air as you breathe it in.

quests.instruction: Time for a sandwich! Which part of your face does the food go into?
quests.hint: It opens wide for a yawn and for a spoonful of soup.
quests.explanation: Eating starts in your mouth, where you bite, chew, and swallow. It also lets you talk, sing, and laugh.
quests.funFact: Babies are born knowing how to suck, which is how they drink milk.

quests.instruction: A friend whispers a secret to you. Which body part catches the sound?
quests.hint: You have two, one on the left side of your head and one on the right.
quests.explanation: Your ears collect sounds from the air and send them inside your head so you can hear, even a quiet whisper.
quests.funFact: The part of the ear you can see is only the outside. Most of your ear is hidden inside your head.

quests.instruction: Before leaving for school, you run a comb through it. What are you combing?
quests.hint: It grows from the top of your head and can be short, long, curly, or straight.
quests.explanation: Hair grows out of your scalp. Combing keeps it neat and gets the tangles out.
quests.funFact: The hair on your head grows about one centimeter every month.

quests.instruction: A hat is made to sit on top of which part of your body?
quests.hint: It holds your brain and carries your eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
quests.explanation: Your head holds your brain and your face. A hat or a helmet sits on top to keep it covered or protected.
quests.funFact: A newborn baby's head is about one quarter of its whole body length. As you grow, the rest of you catches up.

quests.instruction: You pick up a crayon to color a picture. Which body part holds the crayon?
quests.hint: It is at the end of your arm and has a palm on one side.
quests.explanation: Your hands grip, hold, and move things, from crayons to cups. Each hand has a palm, four fingers, and a thumb.
quests.funFact: Your thumb can reach across to touch each of your other fingertips, which makes picking up small things easy.

quests.instruction: Socks and shoes go on which body parts before you go outside?
quests.hint: They are at the bottom of your legs, and they touch the ground when you stand.
quests.explanation: Your feet carry your weight and take you from place to place. Socks and shoes keep them comfortable and safe.
quests.funFact: Your feet have curved arches that soak up the shock when you walk and jump.

quests.instruction: Which body parts help you pick up one tiny bead from the table?
quests.hint: Each hand has five of them, and one is called the thumb.
quests.explanation: Fingers are small, bendy parts of your hand. They pinch, point, and grip, even tiny things like beads.
quests.funFact: Your fingertips have lots of tiny nerve endings, so they are very good at feeling small details.

quests.instruction: You are walking to school. Which long body parts carry you along, step after step?
quests.hint: You bend them when you sit, and they help you stand, walk, and run.
quests.explanation: Your legs are strong, long parts that carry your body when you walk, run, jump, and climb.
quests.funFact: Some of the biggest muscles in your whole body are in your legs.

quests.instruction: Stretch out like an airplane! Which two body parts are spread out like wings?
quests.hint: They reach out from your shoulders and end in hands.
quests.explanation: Your arms stretch from your shoulders to your hands. They reach, lift, carry, and hug.
quests.funFact: Your upper arm has one long bone, and your lower arm has two.

quests.instruction: Which small parts at the end of your foot can wiggle inside your shoe?
quests.hint: Each foot has five of them, and the biggest one has its own name: the big toe.
quests.explanation: Toes help you balance and push off the ground when you walk, run, and jump.
quests.funFact: Your big toe has two bones, but each of your other toes has three.

quests.instruction: Crunch! You bite into a carrot. Which hard, white parts in your mouth do the biting and chewing?
quests.hint: Babies are born without any, and they grow in later.
quests.explanation: Teeth cut and grind food into small pieces that are easy to swallow. Front teeth bite, and back teeth crush.
quests.funFact: Children usually have 20 baby teeth, and adults can have up to 32 teeth.

quests.instruction: You lick an ice cream cone. Which soft, wet part of your mouth sticks out to do the licking?
quests.hint: It is pink, and it also helps you say words clearly.
quests.explanation: Your tongue is a strong, bendy muscle. It moves food around your mouth, helps you talk, and lets you taste.
quests.funFact: The top of your tongue is covered in tiny bumps, and some of them hold your taste buds.

quests.instruction: Which part joins your head to the rest of your body and lets you look left and right?
quests.hint: In winter, you wrap a scarf around it.
quests.explanation: Your neck holds your head up and lets it nod, tilt, and turn.
quests.funFact: A giraffe has seven neck bones, just like you. Each one is much longer than yours.

quests.instruction: After a big dinner, which part of your body feels full and round, and might rumble when you are hungry?
quests.hint: It is on the front of your body, below your chest.
quests.explanation: Your tummy is the soft part at the front of your body, below your chest. Your stomach, which helps break down food, is inside it.
quests.funFact: Tummy rumbles come from food, liquid, and air moving through your digestive tract.

quests.instruction: Where do the straps of your backpack rest?
quests.hint: They sit between your neck and your arms.
quests.explanation: Shoulders are where your arms join your body. They let you swing your arms in big circles and carry things like a bag.
quests.funFact: Your shoulder can move in more directions than most other joints in your body.

quests.instruction: You sit down on a chair. Which part in the middle of each leg bends?
quests.hint: You can feel a round bump at the front when you bend your leg.
quests.explanation: Knees are joints that let your legs bend. That is how you sit, kneel, squat, and climb stairs.
quests.funFact: Your kneecap is a small, round bone that protects the front of your knee.

quests.instruction: Bend your arm like you are showing off a muscle. Which part makes the pointed bend in the middle?
quests.hint: It is between your shoulder and your hand.
quests.explanation: Your elbow is a joint in the middle of your arm. It lets your arm bend and straighten so you can reach, eat, and throw.
quests.funFact: The funny bone is not a bone at all. It is a nerve near your elbow that tingles when you bump it.

quests.instruction: Lie on the floor and look up at the ceiling. Which wide part of your body presses against the floor?
quests.hint: It is on the opposite side of your body from your tummy.
quests.explanation: Your back is the long, wide part along the rear of your body, starting at your neck. It holds you upright and helps you bend and twist.
quests.funFact: Down the middle of your back runs your spine, a stack of small bones that lets you bend and twist.

quests.instruction: Which part is the wide front of your body between your neck and your tummy?
quests.hint: You can feel it rise and fall when you take a deep breath.
quests.explanation: Your chest holds your heart and your lungs, and a cage of ribs protects them.
quests.funFact: You have 12 pairs of ribs, and they move slightly each time you breathe.

quests.instruction: You have two eyes and two ears. Which of these do you have only one of?
quests.hint: Look in a mirror. It sits alone in the middle of your face.
quests.explanation: Many face parts come in pairs, but your nose is in the center. It has two openings called nostrils.
quests.funFact: A thin wall inside your nose keeps your two nostrils separate.

quests.instruction: Hold up both hands and count. You can count ten of which body part?
quests.hint: Each hand has four of them plus a thumb.
quests.explanation: Each hand has four fingers and a thumb, which makes five. Two hands make ten.
quests.funFact: Your fingerprints formed before you were born, and they stay the same all your life.

quests.instruction: Two of these sit side by side, right above your nose. Which are they?
quests.hint: Your eyebrows rest just above them.
quests.explanation: Your eyes sit in round hollows in your skull, which protect them.
quests.funFact: The colored ring in each eye is called the iris.

quests.instruction: A palm and five fingers together make up which body part?
quests.hint: You use them to clap and to shake hello.
quests.explanation: A hand is made of a palm, four fingers, and a thumb, all working together.
quests.funFact: Your two hands hold more than a quarter of all the bones in your body.

quests.instruction: Knees sit in the middle of which two long body parts?
quests.hint: They end in feet, and they hold you up when you stand.
quests.explanation: Each leg has a knee in the middle, with a thigh above it and a shin below it.
quests.funFact: The thigh bone is the longest bone in your body.

quests.instruction: Lips, teeth, and a tongue all belong to which part of your face?
quests.hint: It opens when you talk, laugh, and yawn.
quests.explanation: Your mouth includes your lips, teeth, and tongue. It is where you eat, talk, and laugh.
quests.funFact: Your mouth makes a watery liquid called saliva, which moistens food and begins to break it down.

quests.instruction: Two of these are on your face. Which one is not?
quests.hint: Think about which one bends in the middle of your arm.
quests.explanation: Your eyes and nose are on your face. Your elbow is a joint in the middle of your arm.
quests.funFact: Your face has dozens of small muscles that let you smile, frown, and wink.

quests.instruction: Slide your hand down your body, starting at your head. Which of these do you reach first?
quests.hint: Picture yourself standing. The highest one is closest to your head.
quests.explanation: Going down from your head, you reach your shoulders first, then your knees, and your toes last.
quests.funFact: You are slightly taller in the morning than at night, because the cushions between the bones in your back flatten a little during the day.

quests.instruction: Fingers belong to hands. Toes belong to which body part?
quests.hint: They are at the bottom of your legs, and you wear shoes on them.
quests.explanation: Fingers are at the end of your hands, and toes are at the end of your feet.
quests.funFact: Your big toe does much of the work when you push off the ground to take a step.
